title: How the Motion Explainer VS Code plugin works
summary: The agent authors a walkthrough. File events open or rebuild its offline player in a native VS Code tab, without an MCP service.

watcher.desc: Watches generated index.html files and source edits. The 450 ms debounce groups related saves before rebuilding.

builder.desc: Validates every flow, reuses cached SVGs for unchanged layouts, and creates one offline HTML player.

viewer.desc: A native webview preserves the upstream player. Source references are checked and opened on the workspace host.

flows.label: First explanation
flows.description: The first built walkthrough opens inside the IDE.

steps.say: The coding agent grounds the diagram and narration in source files it has read.
The skill invokes the builder without launching a separate browser.
A new layout is rendered locally. Cached layouts skip this work.
The SVG receives stable node and edge tags so packets can follow the drawn paths.
The builder combines diagram, steps, payloads, and controls into a self-contained player.
The extension sees the generated file change after the build completes.
The same native tab is revealed without taking focus from the coding conversation.

flows.label: Follow-up edit
flows.description: A follow-up changes the explanation and refreshes the existing view.

steps.say: A substantive follow-up updates the actual source of the walkthrough, not just the chat response.
The source watcher waits for related saves before scheduling a rebuild.
Concurrent saves for the same walkthrough are coalesced. Invalid JSON keeps the last valid player visible.
Narration-only changes reuse the cached diagram and produce a fresh player quickly.
The new generated file signals that the follow-up is ready to display.
The existing tab reloads with the new explanation and can start playback.
